sections.html:
South Windsor is a Hartford County town on the east bank of the Connecticut River, with 26,918 residents at the 2020 census. Old Main Street runs near the river and anchors the oldest part of town, and newer subdivisions, shopping areas and industrial parks lie farther east. A nine-member Town Council meets at 1540 Sullivan Avenue.

The town went from 4,066 people in 1950 to 15,553 in 1970, and most of the houses from that wave are now 50 to 70 years old. That is the age when roofs, boilers, windows and septic or sewer connections tend to need money. An owner of one of those houses often has to decide whether to fund the work or sell without it.

Three places are on the National Register of Historic Places: the East Windsor Hill Historic District, the Elmore Houses on Long Hill Road and the Windsor Farms Historic District. If your house is an older one near Main Street, ask the town's land use staff what rules apply before planning exterior changes. Historic status can limit what a buyer is allowed to do, and buyers will ask.

The Connecticut River and the Scantic River border parts of town, so check flood zone status for your parcel with your insurer or lender. Roads matter to buyers too, since U.S. Route 5 and Interstate 291 run along the western edge near the river.

Winters are cold, with record lows of minus 24 degrees, and rain falls in every month. Freeze and thaw cycles work on driveways, chimneys, foundations and roof flashing, and steady moisture makes basements and crawl spaces a common inspection issue.

A vacant or inherited house is the most exposed. Pipes that are not winterized can burst, and a house left unheated for one winter loses value quickly. Keep the utilities on and the roof tight until the sale closes.

Public school students attend one of four elementary schools (Pleasant Valley, Orchard Hill, Philip R. Smith and Eli Terry), then Timothy Edwards Middle School, then South Windsor High School. Buyers with children ask which school serves a street, so put the answer in your notes.

Many buyers at these price points use conventional financing and ask for repairs after the inspection. Some sellers choose a cash sale to skip that step. The town's biggest employer is the town itself, followed by firms such as Broadbridge and New England Mechanical, so a job change or relocation is a common reason an owner needs to move on a deadline.

The seller pays the tax on any deed where the consideration is $2,000 or more. On top of the state rate, the town receives 0.25 percent. Non-residential property other than unimproved land pays 1.25 percent to the state. The statute is Chapter 223, Sec. 12-494.

A town may add a small extra amount if it qualifies under the law, so confirm with the town clerk. Exemptions exist, including a transfer of a principal residence in lieu of foreclosure and a sale where the price does not cover the mortgages and priority tax liens.

The seller, the seller's attorney or an authorized agent files Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded, and the tax is due then. Towns that take part in myCTREC let filers pay electronically, and the bank draft starts only after the instrument is recorded. The deed goes to the town clerk's land records office. Ask the South Windsor town clerk whether the town is on the electronic system and what the recording fee is.

  • Gather the deed, payoff statements and the buyer's name before the closing date.
  • Ask the title or closing attorney to prepare Form OP-236.
  • Confirm that unpaid property tax and sewer charges are paid from proceeds.
  • Keep copies of the recorded deed and the tax return.

Each Connecticut town chooses one, two or four installments a year, and the last must fall at least 45 days before the fiscal year ends (Chapter 204, Sec. 12-142). A late installment becomes delinquent and accrues interest at 18 percent a year, with a minimum of $2 per installment unless the town waives it (Sec. 12-146).

Call the South Windsor Collector of Revenue or the Assessor for the exact due dates and the mill rate. Ask that office, too, whether any sewer or other municipal charges are open on the parcel, so the payoff is correct at closing.

sections.h2: Cash sale for a house that needs work
sections.html:
A cash purchase can close without a bank appraisal or lender repair demands, so a house with an old roof, a failing septic or sewer connection, or deferred maintenance can still sell. The offer reflects the repairs the buyer takes on, which is why it usually comes in below a fully renovated listing price.

A listing may bring more if the house is in good shape and you have months to spare. A cash sale makes more sense when you need speed, privacy or certainty. We buy houses in South Windsor and the surrounding Hartford County towns in as-is condition, and we will explain our number so you can compare it to a listing.

sections.h2: Tenants, liens and what to do first
sections.html:
You can often sell with a tenant in place or a lien on record. Past-due tax or a lien is normally paid from the proceeds at closing, and a tenant should be disclosed to the buyer early. A Connecticut attorney can tell you how the lease and the timing fit your facts.

Start by pulling the deed, your latest mortgage statement and the newest tax bill. Then get the tax balance from the Collector of Revenue and hire a closing attorney. Once those three pieces are in hand, you can compare offers with real figures and pick a closing date.

faqs.q: Is South Windsor in Hartford County?
faqs.a: Yes. It is a Hartford County town east of the Connecticut River, with 26,918 residents at the 2020 census.

faqs.q: Who pays the Connecticut conveyance tax when a house sells?
faqs.a: The seller files the return and pays at recording. The base rate is 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the town, with higher state rates on the part of a residential price over $800,000.

faqs.q: When do late property taxes start charging interest in Connecticut?
faqs.a: An installment is delinquent if it is not paid by the first of the month after it was due. Interest then runs at 18 percent a year back to the due date, with a $2 minimum per installment unless the town waives it.

faqs.q: Can I sell a South Windsor house with a tenant or tax lien?
faqs.a: Often yes. A past-due tax or lien is normally paid from the proceeds at closing, and any tenant should be disclosed early. Talk to a Connecticut attorney about your specifics.

faqs.q: Do I need repairs before a cash sale in South Windsor?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer purchases the house in its current condition, and the repair cost is built into the offer.
